cards.q: Pregnancy test kits: antibody target and what they detect
cards.a: Antibodies to the unique subunit of hCG; qualitative detection within a few days of a missed period

cards.q: Quantitative plasma hCG: method and uses
cards.a: Radioimmunoassay; checks normal pregnancy progress, ectopic pregnancy, mole, choriocarcinoma

cards.q: Thyroid function assays: methods (GG12)
cards.a: Radioimmunoassays, then chemiluminescent and enzyme-linked immunoassays for T4, T3 and TSH

cards.q: Free T4 gold-standard method and its limit
cards.a: Equilibrium dialysis with radioimmunoassay of the dialysate; costly, rarely in routine labs

cards.q: Routine free T4 and T3 assays: principle
cards.a: Labelled iodothyronine analogues in chemiluminescent or enzyme-linked assays; affected by binding proteins and illness

cards.q: Serum TSH: role in thyroid testing with normal pituitary
cards.a: Thyroid function test of choice

cards.q: Digoxin levels: method
cards.a: Radioimmunoassay of serum digoxin

cards.q: Digoxin: concentration range with therapeutic efficacy
Digoxin: concentration linked to increased mortality
cards.a: Above 1.2 ng/mL

cards.q: Urine toxicology screen: how fast it gives results
cards.a: Immunoassay; turnaround about 1 hour

cards.q: Drugs of abuse detected by urine immunoassay screens: list
cards.a: Amphetamines, barbiturates, benzodiazepines, cannabis, cocaine, opiates

cards.q: Limits of urine immunoassay screens
cards.a: False positives from cross-reactivity; long detection windows can mislead about acute toxicity

cards.q: Pharmacokinetics became possible in the 20th century because of
cards.a: Sensitive methods such as high-performance chromatography and mass spectrometry

cards.q: Peptide purification and synthesis advance from the 1970s
cards.a: High-performance liquid chromatography with solid-phase peptide synthesis

cards.q: Metabolomics platforms: list
cards.a: 1H-NMR; liquid or gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry, with chemometric and multivariate analysis

cards.q: Metabolomics: definition
cards.a: Systematic identification and quantification of all metabolites in a sample

cards.q: Metabolomics output in drug development
cards.a: Simultaneous measurement of thousands of chemicals in serum, urine, cells or tissues

cards.q: Metabolites in urine identified by
cards.a: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry

cards.q: Drugs with low safety margin where TDM is useful: list
cards.a: Digoxin, anticonvulsants, antiarrhythmics, theophylline, aminoglycosides, lithium, tricyclic antidepressants

cards.q: TDM is particularly useful in these situations: list
cards.a: Low safety margin; large individual variation; toxic drug with renal failure; poisoning; unexplained failure; compliance checks

cards.q: TDM for long-acting drugs: sample timing for dose adjustment
cards.a: Trough steady-state level, just before the next dose

cards.q: TDM for short-acting drugs (e.g. ampicillin, gentamicin): sample timing
cards.a: Immediate post-absorptive phase, about 1-2 h after oral or i.m. dose, to reflect peak

cards.q: Blood level in poisoning: when to sample and why repeat
cards.a: Earliest sample to confirm poisoning; repeat to estimate clearance and need to hasten elimination (e.g. haemodialysis)

cards.q: Random drug level sampling: use
cards.a: Informative for checking compliance

cards.q: Drugs where plasma level monitoring is of no value: list
cards.a: Antihypertensives, hypoglycaemics, diuretics, oral anticoagulants, inhalational anaesthetics (response measurable); levodopa (activated in body); reserpine, guanethidine, MAO inhibitors, omeprazole (hit and run); organophosphates, phenoxybenzamine (irreversible)

cards.q: Doping detection: androgen other than testosterone
cards.a: Gas chromatography and mass spectrometry, if still taken at testing

cards.q: Exogenous testosterone: first detection method
cards.a: T/E ratio: urinary testosterone glucuronide to epitestosterone glucuronide

cards.q: Why the T/E ratio rises with exogenous testosterone
cards.a: Exogenous testosterone suppresses epitestosterone, so only testosterone is raised

cards.q: Exogenous testosterone: second detection method
cards.a: Gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry of 13C/12C in urinary steroids

cards.q: Isotope ratio result: what a low 13C/12C ratio means
cards.a: Steroid probably from a pharmaceutical source, not endogenous

cards.q: Doping with newer designer androgen: why hard to detect
cards.a: Tetrahydrogestrinone (THG) designed to avoid antidoping detection by structure and rapid catabolism

cards.q: Principle of colorimetry
cards.a: Colour intensity tracks concentration; read from light absorbed at the right wavelength

cards.q: Langendorff cardiac glycoside test: potassium measured by
cards.a: Flame photometry of the coronary outflow

cards.q: Langendorff glycoside test: rise in potassium outflow indicates
cards.a: Positive inotropic effect (correlates well)

cards.q: General ELISA steps in order: list all
cards.a: Coat wells with antigen; block unbound sites; add primary antibody; add enzyme-linked secondary antibody; add substrate forming coloured product

cards.q: Purpose of the blocking step in ELISA
cards.a: Blocks unbound sites to prevent false positives

cards.q: HRP and TMB ELISA: colour after acid and wavelength read
cards.a: Yellow; read at 450 nm

cards.q: Fluorescence polarisation immunoassay (FPIA): principle
cards.a: Fluorescein-labelled drug competes with patient's drug for antibody; more drug means less polarised light

cards.q: Thin-layer chromatography: use and limitation
cards.a: Cheap, quick qualitative purity checks (e.g. alkaloids); only semi-quantitative

cards.q: Toxin analysis methods used qualitatively
cards.a: Colorimetric and UV-visible spectrophotometry

cards.q: Toxin analysis methods used quantitatively: list all
cards.a: Infrared spectroscopy, gas chromatography, HPLC, immunoassay

cards.q: Why radioimmunoassay is now rarely used in clinical labs
cards.a: Radioisotope safety needs; ELISA replaces the radioisotope with an enzyme

cards.q: Flame photometry: emitting species in the flame
cards.a: Excited metal atoms returning to ground state
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Flame photometry: wavelength identifies
cards.a: The element (characteristic wavelength, isolated by a filter)
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Flame photometer: component that feeds the sample into the flame
cards.a: Nebuliser
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Flame photometer: detector
cards.a: Photodetector (signal proportional to intensity)
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Flame photometry: how concentration is found
cards.a: Calibration graph of galvanometer reading vs concentration
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Flame temperature depends on
cards.a: Fuel to oxidant ratio
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Clinical analytes measured by flame photometry
cards.a: Sodium and potassium in serum
refs: WEB Univ of Delhi Chemistry, M.Sc. notes: Flame Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (2023) http://chemistry.du.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Flame-spectroscopy.pdf

cards.q: Radioimmunoassay: nature of the assay
cards.a: Physico-chemical test-tube assay (not a bioassay)

cards.q: Radioimmunoassay: what labelled and unlabelled hormone compete for
cards.a: Limited binding sites of a specific antibody

cards.q: Ratio plotted on the radioimmunoassay standard curve
cards.a: Bound to free (B/F) ratio of labelled hormone, against standard concentration

cards.q: Trend of B/F ratio as unlabelled hormone rises
cards.a: Falls progressively

cards.q: How the unknown plasma level is found in radioimmunoassay
cards.a: Read the B/F ratio off the standard curve run under identical conditions

cards.q: Antibody type from repeated immunisation of animals
cards.a: Polyclonal (monoclonal from hybridoma gives superior assays)

cards.q: Radioisotope used to label the hormone in radioimmunoassay
cards.a: Radioiodine
